# Startup readback: AI-45

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

AI-45 makes evidence and backups recoverable across both PostgreSQL and private R2. The ticket is complete when: (1) the real backup/export records its database/migration checkpoint and linked archive objects with integrity metadata while retaining original file bytes; (2) that backup restores into a clean isolated recovery environment with relational links, trace/evidence retrieval, and SHA-256 file bytes verified; and (3) missing or corrupted objects fail with an actionable integrity result, recovery material stays encrypted/private, and the RPO/RTO and manual recovery path are documented. The required staging proof also repeats a representative read/report journey and records `LIVE E2E SIGN-OFF: PASS`.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-9 is Done; PR #140 merged as `651067cbf9ee1b6296580a38e2e37be65ddcd26f`, establishing release-gated migration and environment parity. AI-19 is Done; PR #171's accepted proof was based on head `01b61d1cf3a0b62ac45ec0608bbff2b3bcc23279` and merged as `daae0525b7a06d897e045390d8d91297d3324276`, establishing trace, audit, evidence, freshness, and archive metadata contracts. AI-65 is Done; its redacted manifest and live evidence verify separate private staging/production R2 bucket canaries, but do not verify application-level archive restore. The operator confirmed the account is limited to staging and production Supabase projects and chose a local isolated recovery target instead of a third hosted project. The hosted staging-recovery path remains guarded and unchanged; the local path uses an isolated local Supabase project plus a loopback-only S3-compatible archive. The staging backup bucket and versioned encryption key are configured for a later staging-source run, which must wait for the release queue. Follow the Build Spec's PostgreSQL operational store/private R2 archive, original-byte preservation, SHA-256 metadata, encrypted backup, and restore-drill requirements; follow the Agent Spec's trace/evidence provenance and Systems recovery ownership. Apply the Frontend Constitution to the MFA-gated archived-evidence retrieval state. Extend existing `source_objects` producers (`finance-import` and `health-ingest`), the private Worker finance R2 gateway, and `trace_events.archive_reference`; `packages/integrations/src/r2.ts` currently provides only an in-memory test adapter. Integration risks: DB-02, DB-03, R2-01, R2-02, ACC-01, OPS-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

The finance gateway previously trusted PUT metadata and returned a database-usable key without a GET/read-back. The R2 write boundary now verifies exact bytes, size, MIME, and SHA-256, and its caller requires the explicit verified marker. An owner-scoped archive download path checks database ownership, consumes a one-time fresh-MFA `archive_read` gate, then verifies private R2 bytes against the stored SHA/size/MIME. The new backup utility captures database/migration metadata and exact referenced R2 bytes in a versioned AES-256-GCM encrypted bundle, with GET/decrypt read-back; production restore is refused. Hosted staging recovery keeps the existing distinct-project and private-bucket safeguards; the local recovery path does not require a third hosted Supabase project. Import the multi-statement SQL from the existing `supabase db dump` producer through `psql` in the verified target container with `--single-transaction` and `--set ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; `supabase db query --file` rejects multi-command dumps. Keep operational rows in PostgreSQL and raw files, large trace payloads, archives, and backups in private R2 with validated references. Recovery credentials and backup secrets must not enter browser code, ordinary logs, test fixtures, or evidence. Use synthetic staging data and an isolated recovery target; never overwrite production or copy production personal data. The confirmed gateway defect is recorded as R2-01 with its regression proof and failure-ledger entry.

## Local tests and commands

Use focused tests for the touched archive/backup boundary: valid encrypted round trip, wrong key/corrupt envelope, missing/extra/truncated/hash-mismatched object, archive PUT/read-back mismatch, owner scoping, MFA gate enforcement, and actionable redacted errors. The confirmed R2 defect was that the gateway accepted the PUT result and emitted a usable archive reference without a subsequent GET; missing or corrupted persisted bytes could pass. Regression command: `corepack pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run 'app/api/internal/finance-archive/route.test.ts' 'lib/archive-gateway.test.ts'`; the tests now require corrupted bytes to return `502 archive_readback_mismatch`, missing read-back to return `502 archive_readback_missing`, and success only after verified bytes and metadata. Earlier local results: 11 archive route/gateway tests pass; five original backup integrity/restore-isolation tests passed before this importer fix; web typecheck and strict backup CLI typecheck pass; both changed Deno functions pass `deno check --no-config`. Migration `20261021131411` applies locally and `corepack pnpm exec supabase test db --local supabase/tests/ai45_archive_restore.sql` passes all 18 assertions. The full `corepack pnpm verify:changed` gate passed before this restore-import change. This change now has 10 focused backup/restore tests passing, including exact-container validation, `psql` error-stop, cleanup and import failure propagation, Windows Corepack invocation, and CLI JSON-envelope parsing. Two defects surfaced in the first real synthetic run: `execFile('corepack', ...)` could not launch the Windows `.cmd` shim (`spawn corepack ENOENT`), and the backup parser treated Supabase's trailing version notice as part of the JSON (`backup_database_query_invalid_json`). Both boundaries now use the established argv-only Corepack and bounded CLI JSON parsers. The isolated two-stack encrypted archive→restore round trip still must prove schema/row/object-hash restoration with the source unchanged.

## Hosted proof and readiness

AI-65's bucket canaries are prerequisites only. No hosted restore has been run. The root release queue owns any staging-source operation; when authorized, use synthetic staging data and the configured staging backup bucket/key, restore to the local target, check row/relationship/hash/trace output, and corrupt only the local disposable object. Keep existing hosted target safeguards and do not provision a third Supabase project. The issue's representative read and `LIVE E2E SIGN-OFF: PASS` remain release acceptance; stop at a headed sign-in/MFA gate for the operator. Production receives only bounded affected-capability smoke; never restore over production.

## Delegation and blockers

One owner is accountable from implementation through merge; no subagent handoff is planned. AI-9, AI-19, and AI-65 are complete and their relevant contracts are available. The parent controls shared migration-prefix and integration-rule coordination and the staged QA schedule. If staging requires a headed login or MFA, stop before sign-in and tell the parent when the browser is ready for the user's action. Current known gates are the ticket-specific isolated restore proof, required CI, merge, and bounded production smoke.

It does not prove the issue's linked trace/evidence or representative application read outcome. Existing approved R2 source and dedicated backup credentials both pass actual HeadBucket checks; no additional hosted Supabase project or operator key is needed. Using existing encrypted backup CLI, private archive retrieval route and canonical release consumer; integration risks R2-01/R2-02 and DB-13. The archive-restore profile now remains pending until staging source capture, encrypted private bundle, isolated restore, linked trace/evidence read, exact file bytes, isolated corruption detection and unchanged source all pass. Next extend the synthetic fixture with actual linked trace/evidence/report state, validate every downstream read before attended staging, integrate current security main, pass selected checks/CI, then request the serialized staging-source lease.
